data.description:
## Context / Problem
Re-running today's code reviewer (`rebar review-code`, attested snapshot) on bug-introducing changes shows findings that name the escaped defect landing at priority 0.60 with validity 1.0 on criteria that cannot block: change `c3aec3eae6` (Gerrit 1560; bug `earthen-flayed-baboon`) produced a `correctness`/`edge-cases` finding that is the exact bug, advisory only because neither criterion has an entry in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` (unknown criteria default to 0.95/off, `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:496-497`); change `d2dea317ec` (Gerrit 1727; three bugs) produced a `concurrency` finding at 0.60 naming a real defect (a stand-aside still stamps the sweep clock), advisory because `concurrency` is routed `blocking_enabled: false` at 0.95. The `tests` and `regression` criteria block at 0.54. The code-v4 friction replay (`61d50b0513`, `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md`) has not been run for these three criteria. Approved 2026-08-21.

## Approach
(1) Add explicit routing entries for `correctness` and `edge-cases` (exec AGENT, posture advisory, threshold 0.95) so their findings are scored and surfaced with provenance rather than falling to the unknown-criterion default. (2) Run the existing v4 friction replay for `correctness`, `edge-cases`, and `concurrency` at 0.54 over the post-08-20 sidecar corpus, with the escaped-bug findings from this review's three re-reviews (and the next two candidates, Gerrit 1492 and 1850, re-reviewed the same way) as a required-recall set; record the would-block count and amended-after rate per criterion in `docs/experiments/`. (3) Flip to `blocking_enabled: true` at 0.54 only for criteria whose replay stays inside the 8% friction budget; leave the others advisory with the measured number recorded. Thresholds are not changed for any currently-blocking criterion.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`, `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration.md` (new section), `tests/unit/llm/code_review/test_criteria_routing.py` (routing parity), `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` allowlist if the criterion ids are new to it.

## Testing
Routing parity and vocabulary gates pass; a unit test asserts `correctness` and `edge-cases` resolve to an explicit entry (not the unknown default). The replay artifact is committed with the per-criterion numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `correctness` and `edge-cases` have explicit routing entries; checked by `pytest tests/unit/llm/code_review -k routing` and `scripts/check_criteria_routing_parity`.
- [ ] The replay document lists, per criterion at 0.54: changes that would block, percent of corpus, amended-after count, and the recall on the escaped-bug set; checked by reading the committed document.
- [ ] Any criterion flipped to blocking shows a replay friction at or under 8%; any left advisory shows its measured number; checked by comparing the routing file to the document.
data.title: Route correctness and edge-cases explicitly and replay blocking at 0.54 for them and concurrency
